title: The Distant Protocol Again
premise: Bram Coldharbour, a terraformer hauling cargo through contested orbits while tending a garden meant for colonists not yet born, intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries. The signal is a survivor's testimony of the Meridian Station massacre—an event every official record insists never happened. As Bram digs into erased archives and attracts the attention of the Concord's memory-enforcement agents, he realizes his own missing years may be tied to the cover-up. In the end, Bram broadcasts the testimony to every unborn-colony ship in the fleet, sacrificing his anonymity and nearly his life, so that justice can live outside the law—in collective memory that cannot be deleted.
about_author: Jonah Brightwater is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They write about ordinary workers caught in machinery far larger than themselves.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. While hauling cargo past contested orbits, Bram tends his seed-vault garden and intercepts a distress beacon broadcasting in extinct Old Meridian. Decoding it, he hears a woman describe a station massacre—dated three days after records claim Meridian was decommissioned empty. The emotional beat is quiet unease curdling into obsession: someone is lying, and Bram can't stop listening.

chapters.title: The Erasure Bureau
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with an intercut from Inspector Veyne of the Concord's Memory Office. Bram smuggles himself toward Meridian's coordinates and finds only vacuum where debris fields should be. Veyne, tracking the illegal signal, flags Bram as a 'narrative contaminant.' The beat is dread and isolation as Bram realizes the massacre wasn't just covered up—it was engineered to be unthinkable.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV at climax. Cornered by Veyne's enforcers aboard his own ship, Bram discovers the seed vault's genetic archive contains tissue samples from Meridian's dead—his terraforming contract was the disposal method, and his missing seven years were wiped when he witnessed too much. He fights free during a boarding action, choosing to burn his cargo rather than let the evidence be reclaimed.

chapters.title: Broadcast for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, closing on Veyne's. Wounded and stripped of his license, Bram hijacks the colony-fleet relay and transmits the testimony, the archive data, and his own recovered memories to every generation ship still in transit—the people the records can't yet touch. Veyne watches the truth propagate beyond her reach. The beat is costly vindication: justice achieved outside the law, paid for with everything Bram had.
